source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

39087.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Brown and Husted, Lawrence County stayed Republican but by far less than in 2024. Trump carried it by 51 points; Husted led 11,023 to 5,961, a 28-point margin. That 22-point move toward the Democrats ranks second among Ohio's 88 counties, all of which moved left, against a typical Ohio move of 17 points and a national one of 14. Similar Ohio counties moved less: Champaign by 19, Pickaway by 17 and Ashland by 16.

Only 18,034 votes were cast, 68% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters who changed their minds and how much from those who stayed home.

With 98% of the expected vote counted, that shift is almost exactly Ohio's typical county move of 17 points, ranking 41st of the 88 counties, all of which moved left. Similar Republican counties moved about as much: Clinton 17, Coshocton 18 and Guernsey 20.

Turnout was much lower than in 2024: 14,685 votes, 73% of the 20,241 cast for president. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Turnout was 82% of the 2024 level, with 105,841 ballots against 128,535, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Portage 18 points, Trumbull 19 and Erie 15.
